clue.text: See 12
Fragrant substance produced when badger scratches head

indicators.note: scratching out the head means striking off the first letter of the word for badger

parts.note: to badger someone is to pester them

explanation.surface: A perfume is released whenever a badger has a scratch of its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratches head' looks like an animal grooming; it means the first letter is crossed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters are organic compounds, many of them with the fruity smells used in perfumes and flavourings.

clue.text: Politician's bearing setting one up for devotion

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
carrying, so the politician holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
a setting is a site, the place where something happens
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician's posture or attitude is presented as raising someone up for worship.
explanation.walkthrough: MP holds SITE and I to give MSITEIP; 'up' turns that over in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietism is intense religious devotion, piety taken seriously or to excess.

clue.text: Fine wine unopened

indicators.note: a bottle unopened here means the word for the wine loses its opening letter

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A wine judged acceptable even though the bottle was never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: TOKAY, a Hungarian dessert wine, drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean all right or acceptable, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Those at the front in detachment lining up and climbing over the hill in Scotland?

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters are written bottom to top
the letters standing at the front of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A detachment of troops lines up and climbs a Scottish hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials give DLUA; 'climbing' turns them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Auld is the Scots word for old, and someone over the hill is old.

clue.text: Under oath, a bond for removal

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting A and the bond under the oath places them after it

parts.note: eff is a euphemistic swear word, an oath
cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: Someone under oath signs a bond that leads to their removal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under oath' reads as a legal phrase; 'Under' only places A CEMENT below EFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Effacement is rubbing out or erasing, the removal of a mark.

clue.text: See 26
A scream muffled by shout for old competitor

indicators.note: wrapped up inside, so the shout surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a cheer is a shout
something hilarious is a riot or a scream

explanation.surface: A scream is drowned out by a shout, perhaps at a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scream' means something very funny, a RIOT, not a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a chariot in races in the ancient world, a competitor of old.

clue.text: A meeting about usual borders getting praise

indicators.note: around, so the meeting is wrapped round the next letters

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: the borders of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A meeting about the usual boundary disputes earns some praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' looks like boundaries in the surface; here it takes just the edge letters of 'usual'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or praise excessively, so it is a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Gradual increase ultimately in diamonds, a thousand in ring

indicators.note: everything so far sits inside the bell sound

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: placed inside, so the letter goes inside the slang for diamonds

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word increase

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A slow rise in the value of diamonds, a thousand of them set in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' puts the final E inside the slang for diamonds, giving IECE; the second 'in' puts that plus M inside the bell sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done piecemeal is done bit by bit, a step at a time, which is gradual.

clue.text: What's answered when one's going woof or oink, say

definitions.meaning: a need to use the toilet, which one answers when one goes
an animal's natural cry, such as a dog's bark or a pig's grunt

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a euphemism for needing the toilet, and read literally it is the cry of a creature in nature.

clue.text: Criticise one of those billed

definitions.meaning: a marsh bird, and birds have bills

explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily; the water rail is a bird, a creature with a bill.

clue.text: Vessel behind it travelling west during wonderful trip

indicators.note: within, so the other pieces sit inside the word for wonderful

parts.note: ace means excellent or wonderful

indicators.note: the vessel comes after the turned word
in an across entry west is leftwards, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquid

explanation.surface: A ship travels west on what turns out to be a marvellous voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests a journey, but it is trip as in tripping a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripping a switch or alarm sets it off, which is to activate it.

clue.text: Guardian site desperate to bandage wound around paper's leader — investigation of some concern?

indicators.note: a bandage wraps round, so the rearranged letters enclose the wound
desperate suggests wild, frantic disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the wound is placed around the next letter

parts.note: a lesion is a wound or injury

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper's website frantically patches up an injury to its lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper's name but is plain anagram fodder; the wound wrapped round P makes LESPION, bandaged by the rearranged letters. A concern is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a business, and spying on a business's secrets is corporate spying, an investigation of a company.

clue.text: Fill out forms with age in green, originally

indicators.note: the original, first letter of the word green
forms as a verb means shapes, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grows plumper, filling out forms as they get older yet still green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' looks like paperwork; it is the anagram signal working on WITH AGE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill out is to become fuller in the body, putting on pounds.

clue.text: Yellow and black half of nut in aromatic plant

parts.note: lemon is a shade of yellow
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: half of the word for the nut, its first three of six letters

explanation.surface: A yellow and black nut sits inside a fragrant plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of ALMOND gives ALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon balm is a herb of the mint family whose leaves smell of citrus.

clue.text: Tons carried by girl, hideous lump to lift a back-breaker?

indicators.note: held inside, so the girl carries the letter for tons

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a wart is an unsightly lump on the skin

explanation.surface: A girl carries tons, while an ugly lump has to be lifted, a backbreaking job.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverbial straw that broke the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial final burden broke the camel's back, so the phrase names the thing that finally makes something unbearable.

clue.text: Engineers told you so!

definitions.meaning: read as '...', the Royal Engineers of the British Army
the exclamation said when proved right, as in '..., I said so!'

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: the Engineers are 'the RE', THE + RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is used triumphantly when one's prediction has come true.

clue.text: Problem supporters backing United

indicators.note: backing means the word fans is read backwards

parts.note: fans are supporters
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: Fans turning their backs on United would be a problem for the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like supporting; it reverses FANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a chaotic mess or foul-up, originally military slang.

clue.text: See 19
Silent voices restored originally, Lebanon rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new order
the original, opening letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: With voices restored, a rebuilt Lebanon is no longer silent.
explanation.walkthrough: V and R join LEBANON, and 'rebuilt' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Communication that uses no words or speech is wordless, so it is silent.

clue.text: Mean when in a temper initially, money handed over in card game beginning to escalate

indicators.note: placed inside the card game

parts.note: brag is a card game related to poker

indicators.note: the initial letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: tin is slang for money
gave means handed over

indicators.note: the beginning letter of the word escalate

explanation.surface: A cardplayer loses their temper while money changes hands and the stakes start to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a player who is 'in' is batting, so 'Mean when in' is a batsman's average; 'Mean' is not stingy here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer's runs divided by dismissals is the arithmetic mean of their scores while at the crease.

clue.text: Small, small, small amount of money invested in tea plant

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the penny goes into the tea

parts.note: P is a penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: A tiny sum of money is invested in tea, with lots of emphasis on smallness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' sounds financial; it only puts P inside TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden flower grown for its scented blooms.

clue.text: Second: first no more!

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: Someone protests that coming second rather than first will happen no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: The command calls a halt, demanding that something cease.

clue.text: Put one in letter box?

indicators.note: placed inside, so the numeral goes into the box

parts.note: a post is a postbox, where letters are left
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to drop one item into the letter box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' looks like the act of posting; it is the definition, as in putting forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward or propose an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Exchange prisoners sent up

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captives are traded and sent upriver, perhaps to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' suggests imprisonment; it reverses POWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A swop, more often spelt swap, is a trade of one thing for another.

clue.text: Not entirely used up, culinary dye

indicators.note: in a down entry, used upward means the hidden letters are read bottom to top
only part of the word is taken, the letters hiding within it

explanation.surface: A food colouring has nearly been used up in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: LINA sits inside 'culinary'; 'used up' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue colouring obtained from it.

clue.text: Modern time, looking back, in roistering and a crash?

definitions.text: Modern time, looking back, in roistering and a crash?

indicators.note: the turned letters sit inside the rearranged ones
a crash is a smashing up, so these letters are broken and reassembled
looking back means these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: new means modern

explanation.surface: Looking back on a recent era of carousing that ended in a financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns NEW plus T into TWEN. The whole clue describes the 1920s, partying ended by the Wall Street Crash of 1929.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s were a decade of boisterous partying that closed with the 1929 stock market crash.

clue.text: Two items of seafood pinched by cat, not one — unfortunately one can't get away with it

definitions.text: unfortunately one can't get away with it

indicators.note: squeezed inside, so the seafood is held by the shortened whip
without, so the numeral is taken out of the whip

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip
I is the Roman numeral for one
an eel and a clam, two creatures eaten as seafood

explanation.surface: A cat steals a couple of pieces of seafood but cannot quite make a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is the cat o' nine tails, a WHIP; minus I it holds EEL and CLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A device locked on a car's wheel immobilises it, so the clamped vehicle cannot be driven off.

clue.text: Best turkey drunk, according to Spooner?

indicators.note: the first sounds of the two words are swapped, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: a turkey is a flop, a failure
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: The finest turkey was drunk, as the muddled reverend might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FLOP TIGHT gives TOP FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The top flight is the highest division or class, so first-rate means the best.
